tags.description: Imperial Japanese Navy seaplane tender (114.8-118m depending on source) sunk 24 September 1944 by US Task Force 38 aircraft in Coron Bay. Wreck lies on port side, upper hull ~22m, deepest section 36m. Sources disagree on whether a torpedo or bomb hits caused the fatal fuel-tank explosion. Advanced wreck diving required.
tags.name: Akitsushima

tags.description: Also known as South Miniloc, this signature El Nido site features a cabbage-coral garden around 12m with large schools of yellow snappers and tuna, plus jacks, barracuda, squid, and cuttlefish in the current-swept blue. Depth range across the site is roughly 5-35m depending on source. Moderate to strong current between Miniloc and Simizu islands.
tags.name: Biet Point

tags.description: El Nido cave/cavern dive site near Matinloc Island. Beyond a single generic travel-guide mention, no site-specific source could be located confirming depth, features, or marine life for this exact site as of 2026-08-22 QA pass; existing depth/type retained but unconfirmed.
tags.name: Cave

tags.description: Southern tip of Matinloc Island in El Nido. Strong currents attract tuna, jacks, and mackerel past coral-encrusted boulders. Only one live, verifiable source found as of 2026-08-22 (travel-palawan.com); earlier-cited divephilippines.com.ph source is no longer reachable, so shark/moray/lionfish claims from the prior description were removed as unconfirmed.
tags.name: Banayan Point

tags.description: Matinloc Island site (also called Picanayas/Pacanayas) with large boulders. Whitetip reef sharks and pelagics are corroborated by multiple mentions. Sources conflict on profile: one operator lists it as a shallow submerged reef (8-15m, all levels); the prior description described a deeper boulder wall to 20m for advanced divers. Depth/type retained pending a stronger source; only one live source confirmed as of 2026-08-22.
tags.name: Bikanayos Rock

tags.description: Port Barton offshore reef, widely described as a snorkeling/shallow-dive site. A 2025 coral-condition survey (rafsreefbrief.com) puts the reef flat at 0-2m with dropoffs beginning around 5m, and notes the reef was significantly affected by the 2024 mass bleaching event with only small patches of healthy Acropora/Montipora remaining. Depth corrected from a placeholder 20m.
tags.name: Twin Reef

tags.description: Port Barton fringing reef. A 2025 coral-condition survey (rafsreefbrief.com) puts the reef flat at 2-3m with dropoffs to roughly 10m, and reports the reef flat is now macroalgae-dominated with an estimated 50%+ of coral damaged or dead, though scattered healthy colonies (including large brain corals) remain along the dropoffs, especially near Cagsalay Island. Low visibility (~5m) is typical. Depth corrected from a placeholder 25m.
tags.name: Fantastic Reef

tags.description: Smallest of Tubbataha's three reef structures, ~20km north of the main atolls. Mushroom-shaped, starting around 7m and dropping past recreational limits (50m+). Named after the Jessie Beazley, a Liverpool-built ship reported to have sunk here in 1872. Fast, unpredictable currents (2+ knots). Grey reef sharks are common; whitetips and occasional hammerheads reported. Barracuda, Spanish mackerel, Napoleon wrasse, unicornfish and surgeonfish schools. Accessible by liveaboard only, roughly March-June.
tags.name: Jesse Beazley Reef
